newsitem.title: DENMARK: France dismisses call for Algeria initiative.
newsitem.headline: France dismisses call for Algeria initiative.

text.p: France's Foreign Minister Herve de Charette on Monday rejected an opposition call for a French intitiative in troubled Algeria, saying that it was a sovereign state that must resolve its own problems.

At a news conference during a visit to Denmark, de Charette was asked for his reponse to a plea by French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin for France to lead the international community in an effort to restore peace to the former French colony.

"Algeria is an independent country and for the moment we think it is the responsiblity of the Algerian people, Algerian leaders, to find solutions to their own problems," de Charette said, before leaving for Sweden.

In an interview published in the left-wing French daily Liberation on Monday, Jospin said that France should launch consultations with its European neighbours and lobby for greater dialogue between Algeria's government and opposition.
"I believe the international community must wake up...Nobody moves in Europe because France does not move," he said.
Algerian Moslem rebels, blamed for bloody 1995 bombings in France, have accused Paris of supporting Algiers' military-led government and threatened bomb attacks on French soil.
Algerian security forces on Sunday prevented a rally by opposition politicians demanding dialogue with outlawed Islamists and an end to bloodshed in the North African country.

The Peace Call group wants a dialogue established between the opposition, including moderate leaders of the banned Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), and the government to end the civil strife which has killed more than 60,000 people since 1992.
Jospin said Paris should speak out, despite the risk, saying France had already been targeted and continuing violence in Algeria would only worsen the danger.

He hit out both at the rebels' "fanatical terrorism martyring the population" and at the Algerian government, saying it intimidated non-violent opponents and was sometimes brutal in repressing the rebels.

"The Algerian government will overcome terrorism, modernise the country and return some hope to the population only if it accepts some evolution and particularly dialogue with democratic forces," he said.

In a speech on Friday, Algerian President Liamine Zeroual accused the legal opposition of having a hidden agenda of surrendering the country to Moslem guerrillas who according to newspapers have killed more than 250 people this month.
